title: One Word, Every Size
concept: KCAW and the Daily Sitka Sentinel report that Sitka's planning commission recommended on October 21st banning data centers in every zone, checked against the City and Borough of Sitka's staff memo, draft ordinance and electric utility annual report, the Fairbanks North Star Borough agenda and Alaska's News Source, and the UAF ACEP guide. A brass-rimmed enamel sign with a face, the Plate, reads DATA CENTER and fits a fridge-size copper box, the Cubby, and a gigawatt block alike. The film follows that one sign across a painted zoning map, a mailbox, a blank ruler, a Cordova powerhouse, a stack of thirty eight towers, two signposts passed by a dashed recommendation board, a hammer and the ruler, an island balance of 120 made against 118 used, a quiet quote, a Fairbanks tick at 5 MW, a cracked sign and one open signal pink tick.

fingerprint.palette: cedar boardwalk, teal harbor fog, chalk cream enamel signs with brass rims, hydro blue water, signal pink tick and stamp ink, a golden break
fingerprint.metaphor: one brass sign that fits every size of thing, stretched until it cracks against a ruler with no marks

palette: cedar boardwalk, teal harbor fog, chalk cream enamel signs with brass rims, hydro blue water, signal pink tick and stamp ink, a golden break
divergence_note: The last four films were an orbital navy plate with a hot pixel, a paper form in a snowy cutaway building, a plumb bob in dark ground, and a calf on a pewter beach. This film is an eye-level rain-day boardwalk town in warm cedar, teal and cream with one signal pink. There is no orbit, no cutaway slice of ground, no desk, no paper creature and no lamp pool. Its world is built of signs, posts, a ruler and a balance. HONEST OVERLAP: its hero is a faced object for the fourth film in a row, but it is rigid enamel with a hinge that stretches, shares the frame with a second faced box and a bird, and is not paper or a sensor.

treatment.winner: The Explainer's Plate that stretches over every size and cracks on the ruler, with the Comedian's gull gag and the 38-stack pullback, the Dramatist's island scene drawn at full strength with the Sadlier-Hart quote held quiet, and the Enthusiast's open tick as the button.
treatment.why: All four pitches converged on one sign that fits every size. The thesis is a SIZE question, so the picture is a sign stretched past its size against a ruler with no marks. The ban's best case gets its own quiet scene and no gag.

angle.thesis: One word covers a fridge and a gigawatt campus, and Sitka's draft draws no size line, so the real choice before the Assembly is where to draw it, not whether to say yes or no.
angle.falsifiable_by: The Assembly record showing a size line was weighed and rejected because even a Cordova size 150 kilowatt box is judged a threat to the island grid, or the Assembly adding its own size line or permit route (then the rule was never stuck on one word), or a recommendation that already sets a demand threshold.
supporting_facts: c12 the draft definition has no size line
c13/c19 Rudas names one kilowatt, one megawatt, one gigawatt under one word, and Cordova already runs a fridge size 150 kW unit at a hydro plant, per the city memo
c9/c10/c11 record peak 26.02 MW, hyperscale typically over 20 MW, one gigawatt about 38 times that peak (our math)
c22 Fairbanks draws its line at 5 MW
angle.counterpoint_honored: c7/c18/c8/c14 The ban's best case gets its own act-three scene at full strength: an island grid with no neighbor to import from, 120 GWh made and 118 used in 2025, a memo that calls a small power hungry facility not entirely unlikely, and Sadlier-Hart's say it loud. Hydro moves with rainfall. No claim of spare capacity. The film narrows honestly: the caution is rational, the open question is whether a ban or a line plus conditions protects the thin margin better.
angle.second_movement: Staff and the sustainability commission both chose a permit (c2,c3,c4) and the commission overrode them, so the fight was never control versus no control. It is which tool keeps control. Then c9: the whole town peaks at 26 MW.
angle.throughline_object: the one word DATA CENTER on a stamped sign/plate that is physically the same plate on every size of thing. States: one plate on a fridge box (Cordova), the same plate stretching over a town-sized load, the plate cracking along a ruler, a ruler with no marks (the draft), and the final state: the ruler with a single open tick, the line not yet drawn.
angle.ai_link_wording: The city memo says machine learning and AI spurred the sector's growth (c6). No AI company or project is in Sitka. AI is the reason the loads got big, not a party to the story.
angle.valence: curious, constructive, respectful of the ban. No villain, no doom, no boosterism. Never say Sitka banned.
angle.one_question: Sitka's rule would treat a fridge and a gigawatt alike, so where should the line go?
runner_ups_lost: Pure local-control foresight praise (Sitka wrote the rule first): folded in as the opening beat, lost as thesis because it doesn't survive the missing size line
Alaska wins enthusiast: a permit door for Cordova-scale compute: kept as the Act 4 option, lost as thesis because it asserts a benefit no source documents in Sitka

hook.frame1: A rainy powerhouse floor where a brass-rimmed sign with a face slams onto a fridge-size copper box and grins, rain spray ringing out, a gull dropping from the rafters.
hook.headline: THE SAME SIGN
hook.loopback: The last frame is the same Plate and Cubby, now hanging from one open signal pink tick on the ruler, the gull's pencil hovering: the sign that slammed on is now asking where the line goes.

open_loop.what: One sign fits a fridge and a gigawatt. Where does it stop fitting? Planted as the gull flaps the Plate onto a hillside block, paid as the film hands the open tick to the viewer.

open_loop_2.what: What is under the tarp beside Sitka's peak tower? Planted as a brass balance stands covered beside the tower, paid when the wind strips the tarp on the island and 120 made against 118 used leaves the beam nearly level.
